title: Dold–Kan normalization equivalence in an abelian category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with sizes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and use simplicial objects [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. A nonnegative chain complex in $\mathcal A$ has objects $C_m$, $m\geq0$, extended by $C_m=0$ for $m<0$, and differentials $\partial_m:C_m\to C_{m-1}$ for $m\geq1$, extended by zero for $m\leq0$, with $\partial_{m-1}\partial_m=0$; morphisms commute with these differentials. For a simplicial object $X$, put $N(X)_0=X_0$ and $N(X)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}\ker(d_i:X_m\to X_{m-1})$ for $m>0$, with differential the restriction of $d_0$. On a simplicial map use its restrictions to these kernels. The functor $N:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{Ch}_{\geq0}(\mathcal A)$ is an equivalence. It has an inverse $\Gamma$ and natural isomorphisms $N\Gamma\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $\Gamma N\cong\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the equivalence identities.
